sentences.text: On Monday, Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

sentences.text: Kurtaj breached Rockstar Games in 2022 whilst he was on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: He was being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to protect him from rival hackers who threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.79m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: At the time, doctors deemed Kurtaj unfit to stand in a traditional trial due to the severity of his autism, so instead he was given what is known as a trial of the facts.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: The jury was asked to determine whether or not he committed the alleged acts - not if he did so with criminal intent.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: In December 2023 the court ruled that he would remain at a secure hospital for life unless doctors deem him no longer a danger.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: A routine assessment late last year deemed that he was now fit to stand a criminal trial which was scheduled to take place at Woolwich Crown Court.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: But Kurtaj pleaded guilty to all offences.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: He sat in the dock with short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt but no tie.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: The now 21-year-old blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his name, and pled guilty to all counts with no visible emotion.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: The proscution described Kurtaj as a 'leading light' in the teen gang Lapsus$ Those included hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: Kurtaj will be sentenced at a later date.
sentences.article_title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty after release from secure hospital

sentences.text: There are currently 300,000 Agniveers serving in India's defence forces For generations of young Indians, joining the armed forces offered something few other jobs did - a steady career, financial security, the promise of a pension after retirement and the pride of serving their country.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: In 2022, the government upended that arrangement, announcing a new reform scheme under which young men and women entering the military would serve for just four years.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Only a quarter would be allowed to stay on permanently.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The rest would return to civilian life with a lump-sum payment, but without the pension and other benefits that had long made military service an attractive career.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Now, as the first batch of recruits prepares to complete its four-year term, the government is offering them a chance to stay longer, in a significant shift in a policy that has been fiercely debated since its introduction.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: On 4 November, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani announced that recruits who failed to secure permanent positions under the Agnipath, or "path of fire", programme would be offered another two years of service at higher pay.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: They would then get a second opportunity to join the regular forces, provided they met the selection criteria.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Gen Subramani said the decision followed feedback from the forces and insisted that Agnipath would continue.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: But the timing is significant.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: More than 18,300 recruits from the first batch are due to complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Officials say the new arrangement will be offered to more than 300,000 Agniveers - as recruits under the scheme are known - currently serving across the army, navy and air force.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Whether future batches will also be covered remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted the defence ministry for clarification.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The ministry has defended , external Agnipath, saying internal assessments found the recruits to be physically fit, motivated and technologically adaptable.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: It also said the scheme had widened recruitment across districts and made the process more standardised.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: But the extension has brought renewed attention to the trade-offs at the heart of the policy - and whether its original ambitions were realistic.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Those selected are trained for months before being inducted into regiments When the government introduced Agnipath, it argued the scheme would reduce the average age of the armed forces, lower long-term salary and pension costs and create a younger, more technologically adaptable fighting force.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: But military experts and opposition leaders have questioned whether a four-year contract could replace what had traditionally been a coveted, long-term career in the armed forces.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: "Being a soldier in the armed forces was a chance for these young men to make a life for themselves, to get their families out of poor or lower-middle-income conditions," says retired Maj Gen Yash Mor, a vocal critic of the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: These concerns were also amplified by the timing of Agnipath's launch.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Recruitment had been suspended for nearly two years during the Covid pandemic, leaving thousands of aspirants waiting for vacancies to reopen.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The changes were greeted by massive protests across the country, with many saying the career path they had spent years preparing for had fundamentally changed.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: This sentiment was felt most in states and cities that have traditionally been major recruitment hubs, where military service has been a family tradition for generations.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Kulbeer Singh Chaudhary, who runs a recruitment training institute in Dehradun city, says interest in joining the armed forces fell sharply and he stopped conducting Agniveer training batches.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The latest announcement, he hopes, would reverse that trend.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: "The possibility of a longer engagement and eventual absorption into the forces may offer young candidates greater assurance," he says.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: The changes also come at a time when the armed forces are facing personnel shortages.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: In November last year, The Indian Express reported , external that the army alone faced a shortfall of nearly 180,000 soldiers and was considering increasing recruitment.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Many young men from small towns spend months preparing for the selection process to join the defence forces But the debate over Agnipath goes beyond what happens to recruits after four years.
sentences.article_title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

sentences.text: Critics also question whether that is enough time to turn them into experienced soldiers.

sentences.text: So shouldn't you get the best bang for your buck?" he asks.

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Pat McFadden said that "appalling" stories of "abuse of power by powerful men" have emerged this week.

sentences.text: A woman who alleges she was raped by jailed comedian Brand when she was 16 is now campaigning to see the law changed so that relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal.

sentences.text: Questions over a staggered age of consent have "been raised and will be discussed" McFadden said, adding: "[I] can't tell you what the conclusion of that would be, but the last week has certainly put that up in lights." sentences.text: This video can not be played Listen: The distinctive Blackburn 'R' sound Scientists have observed "hidden" tongue movements in one of the last places in England still using a distinctive pronunciation of the letter R and they also witnessed a decline in the historical sound.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: By using ultrasound technology, Lancaster University researchers have been able to watch how the tongue moves during speech.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: The rhoticity study focused on people in Blackburn, as its older  residents still pronounce a "strong R" sound after vowels in words like star and heart.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: Dr Danielle Turton, who led the research, said the findings were "fascinating" as she witnessed the centuries-old sound "gradually disappearing" as the younger generations who took part had much weaker tongue movement.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: Dr Danielle Turton says the study was "so fascinating" as you could see the difference in tongue movements between generations "really clearly" Dr Turton told BBC Radio Lancashire : "East Lancashire is one of the last places in England where people are [distinctively] pronouncing the 'R' sounds.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: "The younger people were making weaker tongue movements.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: They were still doing that traditional Lancashire 'R' but they didn't have the strong tongue movements the older people were making." She said it had been a fun study, adding it was the last sound acquired when learning to talk.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: "We think of language change as something that happened hundreds of years ago but this research we can see that change happening right before our eyes in people's mouths," she said.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: The study focused on Blackburn as Dr Danielle Turton said it was one of the last places in England still using a distinctive pronunciation of 'R' Dr Turton said English had changed beyond recognition over the past 1,000 years which was evident in "Shakespeare, Chaucer and particularly older texts such as Beowulf".
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: "However, language isn't just something that changed in the past.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: It is changing all around us, all the time, in such small increments that we rarely notice it happening." "We can never observe language directly inside the brain, but we can get physically one step closer by observing the movements that create speech," she said.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: "Ultrasound allows us to see tongue movements that would otherwise be completely hidden.
sentences.article_title: Lancashire's 'strong R' due to hidden tongue movement, study finds

sentences.text: "What's exciting here is that we can actually monitor the physical movements involved in a sound change that's happening today." The work forms part of a growing body of research using articulatory imaging to understand how accents change over time and how speech is produced across different communities.

sentences.text: The government has been accused of dragging its feet on its manifesto promise to ban the import of hunting trophies.
sentences.article_title: MPs urge Labour ministers to get on with trophy hunting ban

sentences.text: Labour pledged at the 2024 general election to outlaw bringing the parts of animals killed by hunters for sport, such as heads or horns, into the UK.
sentences.article_title: MPs urge Labour ministers to get on with trophy hunting ban

sentences.text: But it has so far failed to bring a bill enacting the ban to Parliament, and in the two years since the election more than 40 import permits have been granted for hunting trophies.

sentences.article_title: MPs urge Labour ministers to get on with trophy hunting ban

sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.article_title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers

sentences.text: PM Andy Burnham was the only G7 leader to go to COP31 Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned that the consensus on both science and climate change has "gone".
sentences.article_title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'

sentences.text: Addressing other world leaders and delegates at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, he said that despite this, the UK was ready to begin a "new era of British leadership" on the climate change issue.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'

sentences.text: But environmental campaigners at the summit said the PM had to back up his warm words with stronger actions.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'

sentences.text: Burnham opened his speech on Thursday by talking about the heat experienced in the UK this past summer.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'

sentences.article_title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'

sentences.text: Alessandri, the former head of the Joint Intelligence Committee, said: "Climate change and nature loss are increasingly shaping the security environment in which the UK operates." sentences.text: Andy Burnham has signalled his support for dedicated options at the next census to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: It comes after Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde called for legislation to widen ethnicity options for respondents at the next population count, due in 2031.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The last census, held in 2021, saw English offered within a broader white category, but without specific options for black English or Asian English.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Asked at Prime Minister's Questions whether he would support Babarinde's proposal, Burnham said he had not seen details of the plan.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: But he added: "I stand here thinking that I would want to support that bill, to directly take on the poisonous politics we've seen from some in this House".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: "We must bring people back together.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: I am interested in working with anyone in this House who shares that aim," he added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Burnham did not respond to a follow-up question from Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey about whether he would meet Babarinde to discuss his plan, and he did not specify whether the government would give it time for debate in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Babarinde introduced his proposal for legislation on Tuesday, under a rule that allows MPs to propose new laws in a 10-minute speech.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Such draft laws, known as private members' bills, rarely become law without support from the government of the day but are often used by MPs to raise awareness of issues and generate media attention for policy ideas.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP Respondents to the 2021 census were asked a two-stage question about ethnicity, with options grouped under five broad ethnic headings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: In Wales, the terms "Asian Welsh" and "Black Welsh" were listed in the broad categories themselves, and respondents were able to pick "Welsh" as an option underneath the broader white category.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The form in England listed "English" as an option in the white ethnic category, but the only way for respondents to describe themselves as Black English or Black English was via a free-form text box.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: In Scotland, the term "Scottish Asian" appeared in the broad categories, whilst "Black Scottish" was given as an example response for the text box.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Speaking on Tuesday, Babarinde said his proposed law would introduce Black English and Asian English as specific new categories, arguing that the text box on the current form "may as well be the margin".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Babarinde's proposal has been backed by some MPs in other parties, including Labour former deputy prime minister David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly, who quit the shadow cabinet this summer to run for London mayor.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The Eastbourne MP has previously told the BBC he put forward his bill in the wake of comments by former Conservative home secretary Suella Braverman, who defected to Reform UK earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Braverman wrote in 2015 , external that she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: She has reaffirmed her position in recent weeks, writing on X that Englishness was "an ethnicity" and it was "not racist to say this".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: "To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: It also denies me my Asian heritage," she added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The detailed questions asked during the census in England and Wales are set out in legislation following recommendations from the Office for National Statistics (ONS).
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The ONS told the BBC that the Government Statistical Service has been working on a new approach to asking about ethnicity in official surveys since 2022, with an update on the work due to be published on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: That could lead to a recommendation to change the ethnicity question at the 2031 census, although the questionnaire itself is normally designed much closer to the time the census is due to take place.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Legislation setting out the questions for the last census was published in summer 2020, ahead of it taking place in March the following year.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The Scottish government delayed the census in Scotland until 2022 because of the Covid pandemic.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Chris Cash says counter-terror officers entered his bedroom and arrested him A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The two men consistently maintained their innocence.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said he denied any wrongdoing and that he had been "unfairly subjected to a trial by media".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He said he had provided reports to a Chinese company, which he believed had clients seeking to develop trading links with the UK, and those reports contained no classified information and relied on public sources.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash returned to the UK in 2019, saying in his resignation message for his job in China that he felt "guilty sitting back and participating in a system that I am uncomfortable with".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He later became the director of a small policy group run by China-sceptic Conservative MPs in Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Berry stayed in China writing reports for a large consultancy which, like many Chinese companies, has links to the government.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: England and Wales' top prosecutor said the case had collapsed last autumn because government officials could not say China had been classed as an "enemy" at the time.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: This prompted accusations of UK political interference to placate the Chinese government.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: China has previously called the allegations of spying "pure fabrication and malicious slander".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The most striking section of the messages handed to the BBC concerns Berry's account of his meeting in summer 2022 with a senior Chinese official who wanted to have "a more detailed co-operation".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In voice notes Berry describes how, beforehand, work colleagues had told him the official's interest had been piqued by reports Berry had written, which included details of the UK's foreign policy approach to China.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The experience "felt like a psychological game of chess" and "like a test", Berry says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He kept his hands under the table as tea was served: "I didn't want it to be obvious if I was nervous.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: I tested to see if my hands were shaking first, then drank the tea." Berry describes the senior Chinese official asking via an interpreter "about the situation in the UK at the moment, about the Tory leadership thing".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: At that time, Boris Johnson had just resigned as the UK's prime minister, and a Conservative leadership battle was taking place, which Liz Truss would go on to win.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry says he jokingly tried to ask his host which candidate China wanted, but the interpreter did not translate his question.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "And then the main guy just shakes my hand like it's time to go," Berry tells Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: After receiving the voice notes, Cash replies via text the next day: "You, my friend, have just been elite captured" before adding: "You're in spy territory now".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In many media reports these particular messages, previously released in a government witness statement, have been presented as a smoking gun - evidence that Cash knew his friend was passing on information to the Chinese state.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But Cash insists it was a "tongue-in-cheek joke" because he knew his friend to be "a staunch critic of the Chinese Communist Party".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The next morning, he made a joke about Berry spying for the UK and getting in trouble with the Chinese authorities, he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash texted: "Keep him sweet… We may have a use for you yet".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I didn't believe he was knowingly spying on the UK through me," says Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I trusted my friend… I wish I had seen the danger earlier, spotted it and cut off all contact." So who was the mystery official Berry had met?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I found out who this guy is," Berry text-messaged Cash a few hours later.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Bigger deal than I thought." Berry posted a link to the Wikipedia page of Cai Qi, who at the time was one of China's most influential politicians and is now, in effect, President Xi Jinping's chief of staff.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry identified Cai Qi (left) as the man he had met - a trusted aide of Chinese President Xi Jinping Whether Berry correctly identified his host remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He has since disputed the suggestion that he met someone as senior as Cai Qi.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: What is beyond dispute is that he believed he may have met someone highly placed within the Chinese political system.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: For Chris Cash, this unusual encounter did not prompt alarm bells.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Asked why not, Cash tells the BBC: "Because I didn't think anything of the meeting, really." We ask Cash why his friend might have been asked to such a meeting.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Strange things happen in China... you know we would often brush shoulders with sort of quite senior members of the Chinese communist party," he tells us.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Challenged about whether he had read the Wikipedia link at the time, Cash says he had "skimmed it", adding that it described him as a judge and a provincial-level official.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I just thought it was a weird meeting with a guy who'd taken an interest," he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Six months later, Berry said in text messages that "off the record" he had it "on pretty good authority" that China was considering dropping sanctions against Tom Tugendhat, one of the Conservative MPs in the China Research Group, where Cash worked.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Berry wrote that this would happen as long as the West "continued to show signals that they are willing to work together".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The Chinese believed it would be "extremely embarrassing" if Tugendhat became prime minister or foreign secretary while under Chinese sanctions, Berry said.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: At the time of the meeting in summer 2022, China-sceptic Tugendhat was seen as a possible contender to succeed Boris Johnson, or become UK foreign secretary.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He was actually appointed as security minister by Liz Truss, and Beijing lifted sanctions on him in January 2026.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Was Cash concerned that Berry appeared to be passing information to him about Chinese foreign policy?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he assumed Berry had heard this "through the grapevine at his company" which was doing business with the UK.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He says he never doubted his friend's trustworthiness, to the extent he even named Berry as a reference on his application for a security pass for the Palace of Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The pass was granted and, a fortnight before their arrests in early 2023, Cash invited Berry to Parliament for lunch.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: It was to be their final face-to-face conversation.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash was in bed at quarter to six on a March morning when he was woken by car doors being shut, he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Within seconds, four UK counter-terrorism officers had barged into his bedroom at his parents' home in Edinburgh.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "They told me to sit up and not touch anything and then said I was under arrest for breaching the Official Secrets Act," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I was in complete shock… quivering...
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: My mum was hysterical." Cash says the officers dressed him in dirty clothes he had worn that weekend, handcuffed him and marched him down to an unmarked police car.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He was later driven to London.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Chris Berry was also arrested the same day.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: It remains unclear how, when and why British security services became interested in the exchanges between the two friends.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But they are likely to have found out far more about their relationship when Berry was stopped and questioned by counter-terror officers at Heathrow Airport.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The allegations were based on 6,273 messages between the pair - the same ones Cash has now shared with the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash's solicitor has told the BBC they are genuine.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: They cover a period when Cash had joined the China Research Group (CRG), founded by Tugendhat and fellow Tory MP Alicia Kearns, and when Berry was working for a Chinese company called Strong, where part of his work involved writing political and economic reports for clients.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: According to court documents, Berry was said to have compiled 34 reports for a man linked to the Chinese state spy agency, relaying information passed on to him by Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Strong did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The CRG's office was across the Thames from Westminster, but Cash regularly had meetings in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash did not have government security clearance and there is no evidence he had access to classified documents.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Despite being thousands of miles apart, the two friends remained in close contact, often messaging daily.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: The messages reviewed by the BBC show them discussing topics including sanctions on China, the tech company Huawei, human rights, Hong Kong, Taiwan and British foreign policy.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he used the Signal app for almost all his contacts with people in China - "more for their protection" - as he says discussing the government "could land someone… in trouble".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He and Berry did not use the app's "disappearing messages" function.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Much of the information they discussed was publicly available, says Cash - who has given the BBC a detailed spreadsheet with links and references in an attempt to prove it.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But sometimes he did share with Berry his impressions from meetings and private discussions in Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: On 12 occasions in the messages, he labelled information "off the record" or "very off the record" before passing it on.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says this was "just me excitedly sharing things that I was doing with him at work".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: One message recounted views allegedly expressed in private by Britain's then-ambassador to China, Dame Caroline Wilson, during a discussion with the CRG about its work on China's influence on UK universities.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash also messaged Berry sharing unverified rumours about the sex lives of two UK cabinet ministers.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: There is no evidence Berry passed this to his Chinese colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash says he regarded such exchanges as routine political discussion.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "We weren't working with classified information," he says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash was told by his solicitor the police investigation would blow over after six months and he would soon be able to return to normal life.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But in September 2023 - six months after the arrests - the case became public when the Sunday Times broke the story of an unnamed "spy" who had been arrested in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash recalls travelling on a train while, around him, fellow passengers read the  newspaper's front page story: "Commons 'Chinese spy' arrested".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He says: "I wanted the world to eat me up." Within 24 hours he was named and pictured in the press, and both men were later charged with espionage.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: In September the following year, just weeks before their trial was due to begin, Cash received an unexpected call from his solicitor.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "Are you sitting down?" he asked Cash.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "They've dropped all the charges." His lawyers requested a court hearing for the prosecution to formally acknowledge that they would offer no evidence, but at the Old Bailey the newly-innocent Cash struggled to find anyone interested in his story.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash's life has changed almost beyond recognition, he says, but he is positive about the future At every previous court appearance he had been mobbed, but the press had not been informed about this hearing.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Eventually his team found a lone BBC journalist.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I said my piece outside the Old Bailey.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: And that was a real high point.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: I felt that I could start to move on with my life." It wouldn't be that simple.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Across the city, House of Commons Speaker Lindsay Hoyle was seething.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It is this Parliament that has been spied on," he declared.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It is MPs' offices that have been infiltrated." There would be days of political debate and a raucous prime minister's questions where Tory leader Kemi Badenoch would claim: "This all stinks of a cover-up." "I'd been acquitted by law, but then I was traduced in Parliament," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It was almost like I was convicted in the court of public opinion again, by people who I had worked with and trusted and that felt horrible." Today Cash's life is almost unrecognisable.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He has lost his dream job, his relationship, and his closest friend from university.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "We talked about being each other's best men," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Instead, when the friend got married last year, Cash was not even invited.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He is also no longer in contact with Berry.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I've been applying for basic admin jobs and having trouble recently," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I'm angry and upset with how everything played out, and I do feel let down." But when asked, Cash stops short of saying he feels Berry betrayed him.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Does he think his friend was spying for the Chinese government?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "He would have to have his time in court to defend himself," Cash answers.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I think it'd be wrong of me to speculate and hypocritical given the speculation that I've been subject to.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But we're no longer friends." Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said his reports "concerned economic and commercial issues widely discussed in the UK at the time and drew on information freely in the public domain".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Like his former friend, Chris Cash is innocent in the eyes of the law, but his reputation has undoubtedly been trashed.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Many in Parliament still think they were spies.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: And with more of the messages between these former friends now revealed, the debate over their actions could be reignited.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It was a gruelling ordeal," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "But I'm a fundamentally positive person… I'm positive about what the future holds." Get in touch – politicsinvestigations@bbc.co.uk , external

sentences.text: Successive governments have been "asleep at the wheel" on adult social care, says the head of the independent commission looking into the sector in England.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: Baroness Louise Casey said care services for older people and adults with disabilities had been developed in a largely uncontrolled and unintended way, unlike the deliberate design of the NHS in 1948.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: As a result, she suggested a postcode lottery had developed with different levels of services available depending on where people live.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: And she also highlighted the fees that self-funders pay, saying they were much higher than councils were charged for people entitled to state support.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: Baroness Casey said care services, such as home adaptations and personal care like helping people out of bed and with washing, were simply not valued enough.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, she said the NHS had become a "national hospital service: that was focussed on medical care".
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: And she said the failings identified by the recent Covid inquiry report into social care were testament to that.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: Last month the inquiry published a report which said the care sector appeared to be " something of an afterthought" in the early stages of the pandemic, allowing Covid to spread like "wildfire" .
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: Baroness Casey, who will address a conference of social care leaders later on Wednesday, said the findings were "so awful" and "a national shame".
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: "Successive governments have been asleep at the wheel.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: We've got our heads in the sand." Her final recommendations for services for older people and adults with disabilities, including care homes, will be published next summer.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: It comes as her commission publishes research showing England is an international outlier for having no "clear system of stewardship" for social care, unlike countries such as France and Germany.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: She said the market was dominated by private providers and said the regulator – the Care Quality Commission – as being a "spectator at the site of a car crash".
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: "Together, we can build a new settlement for care," Baroness Casey said.
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: "One based on values I still believe this country shares – decency, contribution and a duty to care for our neighbours, our loved ones and ourselves." Are you affected by the issues raised in this story?
sentences.article_title: Governments 'asleep at the wheel' over social care, says head of review

sentences.text: A review by Alan Milburn (left) could create political headaches for Andy Burnham Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He saw how last year's welfare rebellion marked the beginning of the end for his predecessor in Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Sir Keir Starmer's authority was shredded when 120 - more than a quarter - of his own MPs threatened to derail his reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: To defuse this, Sir Keir was compelled to guarantee that existing claimants of personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales, wouldn't lose out.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Even then, 49 of the 120 potential Labour rebels still voted against their own government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Next week, a review from former New Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn has the capacity to create another internal row in Labour's ranks.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn has spent a year grappling with how to reduce the nearly one million young people who are not in employment, education or training (Neets).
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: In an interview with the Times, he has now confirmed he is set to recommend cutting benefits for some 16-24 year olds who currently receive Pip, or the enhanced health-related payment of Universal Credit.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Taking benefit cuts to the Parliamentary Labour Party would usually have a similar effect to adding phosphorus to water.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But from my soundings, the deep waters of the Labour ranks are calmer than might be expected.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Importantly, two of the most effective organisers of last year's welfare rebellion are batting for the current prime minister, rather than against the previous one.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Louise Haigh is now the most powerful cabinet minister after Andy Burnham himself, while Anneliese Midgeley is his chief whip.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And the MP who fronted that rebellion - Meg Hillier - has said she wants to give Milburn's proposals a "fair wind".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There are also clear differences to the previous approach to welfare reform.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: First, it is not being presented as primarily a cost-cutting exercise with pre-determined savings.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Instead, there will be upfront investment to provide more support to unemployed young people, and a timeframe for net savings likely to be set at around a decade – gradualism, not a short, sharp shock.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Second, last year's initial reforms would have affected people in all age groups, whilst benefit cuts this time would be limited to the under 25s, who make up around 11% of Pip claimants.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say One in eight young people still out of work or education ahead of major review I've spoken to government ministers who had expressed concerns – at least privately – about the changes devised previously by Rachel Reeves and Liz Kendall.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: This time, they are on board.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One of them told me that so long as there was enough support for young people, with guaranteed jobs and training, MPs would be "fine" with some benefit cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But they added that it was vital that those who really couldn't work wouldn't be worse off.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn will suggest there could even be enhanced payments for people in this category, while some young people with disabilities who lose out on Pip could nonetheless be given an additional "allowance" to help with living costs.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Another minister who opposed the previous reforms praised the process this time.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: There had been a high level of engagement not just from Milburn, but Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden, who has been taking MPs through the principles behind the reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: One minister was a little more cautious, suggesting support for a reduction in benefits would depend on what the entire "package" of reforms looked like.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Milburn's recommendations are likely to be wide-ranging – from pre-school policies to how the NHS deals with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Some of the eventual 49 rebels from last year are in a similar place.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: York MP Rachael Maskell told me it was essential that she saw the detail of the proposals rather than the "drip, drip" of press reports which would "cause young people stress and distress".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She felt withdrawing Pip from young people was "like a sledgehammer to crack a nut" and was concerned that some disabled people required it to remain in work.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: She also suggested that the government "shouldn't just point the finger at young people," and should look closely at how employers could take more youngsters on.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Stroud MP Simon Opher also voted against the government on welfare last year.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He told me there was a "crisis" with so many Neets, and Milburn had come up with a "credible solution".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But he believes cutting benefits should be a "last resort" and is worried about restricting access to the health element of Universal Credit, as a quarter of young claimants aren't Neet.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: He concludes that the "devil will be in the detail".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So much of politics - like comedy – depends on timing.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: For some sceptics, including serving ministers, the Milburn proposals will be more warmly welcomed if support for young people is in place before entitlements are withdrawn.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But for some Labour MPs, cutting payments to existing claimants crosses a line.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Clapham and Brixton Hill MP Bell Ribiero-Addy has she wasn't sure she could back cuts.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Referring to Pip, she didn't believe that "you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: And another MP on the left of the party, Brian Leishman, told the BBC he couldn't back benefits cuts as "we are in the middle of a cost of living crisis".
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: So a welfare rebellion seems guaranteed if Burnham accepts Milburn's recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: But it seems unlikely to be of the same scale, or have a similar level of political jeopardy to the one which shook the Starmer government.
sentences.article_title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?

sentences.text: Cerys and Patrick have different opinions on whether Wales should remain within the United Kingdom in the future Cerys and Patrick have a lot in common.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: They're both young, Welsh, and very interested in politics.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: The one thing they don't agree on is Wales' future within the United Kingdom.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: A leading academic said the conversation around Welsh independence "has become normalised" amongst young people.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: This week, the Plaid Cymru Welsh government set up a new body to consider the case for Welsh independence, as well as more devolution for Cardiff Bay.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: For Patrick, he thinks his country is better off in the UK with more devolved powers, while Cerys believes an independent nation could offer more opportunities to people.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: Nationalist party Plaid formed a government in Wales for the first after winning 46 seats during the May 2026 Senedd election .
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: While it hasn't called for a referendum on independence, the second line of its constitution says: "As the National Party of Wales, the party's aims shall be: to secure independence for Wales in Europe." Pro-union party Reform UK is the second biggest in the Senedd after winning 34 seats in May's election.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: Its Welsh leader Helen Jenner said voters "do not want to see Wales ripped out of the United Kingdom" and said the commission was "ridiculous".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: This video can not be played Young, Welsh and torn on independence A recent poll by Survation for the pro-independence group YesCymru suggested people under 35 in Wales were more in favour of independence than their older peers.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "People feel left behind, especially my age," said Patrick, a 20-year-old student from Newport.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: He added that he could understand why people were "energised and enthusiastic" about independence because of issues such as "student loans, the cost of living, the geopolitical scene".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: But he said: "As of right now, I just do not think there is a case for it." However, Patrick, said he would support further devolved powers for Wales within the union.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: He said that "practical elements" such as whether there would be a border between Wales and England remain unanswered questions for him.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: In Case You Misssed It - Young, political and torn on the future of the UK Are younger Welsh voters driving a shift towards independence?
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: We examine why support is rising among under-35s, hear arguments from both sides and ask what the political future of Wales looks like.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: For Cerys, learning to speak Welsh as an adult and broadening her understanding of history led to a "realisation" that Wales "in reality deserved a lot better than we had been given in the past and in the present".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "I think if we were independent, we could offer people more opportunity here," said the 35-year-old from Bridgend.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: She added she'd like Wales to have further powers over policing and justice - a policy area currently controlled by Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "People seem to be kind of dangling the carrot of more devolution and never actually giving it to us," she said.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "More powers would be great but I will believe in those powers when I see them and until then, I think our best option is independence." Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously said he was open to the idea of giving the Welsh government control of policing in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: Cerys recently spoke at an independence rally in Aberystwyth alongside Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth A leading academic from Cardiff University said "it's staggeringly important" that "young people are a majority in favour of independence".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "They see nothing strange or impossible about Wales becoming independent in the future," said Prof Laura McAllister, from the Welsh Governance Centre.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: She said that there was "great scepticism" around the topic when you look at the opinions of people aged over 65, adding there was a "real demographic schism".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "There's going to need to be something much closer to support at least half the population supporting independence before there is any chance of a referendum being won," McAllister believes.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: She added nobody "can afford to be complacent about the future of the union" because "the concept of the United Kingdom has no God-given right to survive in its current form".
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence

sentences.text: "What we've seen in politics in recent times is that the potential for change is intrinsic to everything that happened," she said.
sentences.article_title: Young, Welsh and into politics - but with different views on independence
