sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.

sentences.text: Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But he said the more robust measures recommended under the new guidance would "come at a cost".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said the latest guidance "does at least provide some clarity", but added that school leaders "cannot simply make mobile phones disappear".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Old landfill and industrial sites have been major sources of the chemicals in rivers like the Mersey Levels of the two most toxic "forever" chemicals in England's rivers have dropped by nearly a third over the last decade, according to new figures from the Environment Agency (EA).
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The decline in the chemicals, PFOS and PFOA, has been put down to stricter restrictions on their use in products after increasing evidence emerged of their damaging impact on human health and the environment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One expert studying the impact of the chemicals said it was "brilliant" to see how far the UK has come on this issue.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Thousands of other forever chemicals, known officially as PFAS, remain in use but the regulator said its report showed the need for them all to be better monitored and regulated.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: PFAS were first developed in the 1930s in the US and became popular with companies making products like frying pans and firefighting foam because of their useful, oil-resistant, water-resistant and electrical properties.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: They are called forever chemicals because their natural resistance means they take a very long time to break down naturally.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The earliest types of these chemicals were called PFOS and PFOA.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: But two decades ago researchers started to find that they were linked to tissue damage in animals and increased rates of certain serious health conditions such as testicular cancer. , external As a result, PFOS was all but banned in the UK in 2010 and PFOA in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The latest data from the regulator, published on Thursday, shows that the concentrations in English rivers of PFOS and PFOA over the last 10 years have now fallen by 30% and 29% respectively.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: Levels in freshwater fish have fallen 49%.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "It's brilliant to see how far we have come in the last 10 years," said Dr David Megson, reader in environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: There are thought to be around 15,000 other PFAS, although only around 200 are frequently used.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA said that despite increasing research into these compounds, "uncertainty remains regarding the toxicity of many PFAS".
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: It said its findings "reinforces the need" for regulating all PFAS rather than one by one.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The chemicals industry has long opposed such an approach, arguing that there is currently no, or limited, evidence to suggest that other PFAS are toxic and that some have vital uses such as in life-saving medical equipment.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The regulator is now regularly testing for 60 other PFAS to build a picture of contamination across the country, and earlier this month the government announced that it would begin monitoring levels in people's bodies.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: The EA report acknowledged that while concentration levels had fallen, because the chemicals take so long to break down, the overall amount still in the environment is likely to have remained unchanged - they have simply been diluted and been washed into the sea.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: "There is a lot to do, and this report provides an essential foundation to support investigations to make the polluters pay for any damage they have caused," said Megson.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: One of the few ways to permanently destroy PFAS is by high-temperature incineration - there are currently just two such suitable sites in the country.
sentences.article_title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Jojo's keeper Maxe Anaclet Makaba: 'He definitely feels lonely - you can see it in his eyes' Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat – to interact with us," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Éric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He definitely feels lonely," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When Jojo first arrived at the sanctuary after spending years in a small iron cage, he didn't look directly at people Jojo is one of the more than 6,000 African primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says. , external Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "If they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist Tony King, from UK charity the Aspinall Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "You see it in their eyes – the light goes out.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas." King – who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes – remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They were clinging to each other," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But Jojo's case is unusual.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film Jojo's face.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: It's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When any primate – a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," Forrester says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: The bonds between gorillas – what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds Dr Robin Morrison from the University of Zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: No one knows how Jojo will react to a companion.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully – perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: These slow, cautious ape introductions do happen – when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Encounters between two or more separate gorilla groups are complex social events The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Prof Forrester studies Jojo as part of research to understand how our understanding of human mental health - particularly stress and trauma - can be applied to our great ape relatives Being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own." Solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, Morrison believes.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females." But while those phases – of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Morrison believes Jojo is probably both traumatised and lonely.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "[In the wild] gorillas move together, find food together, sleep together," she says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "So much of their lives is just being with this group." That is what Jojo's keepers, Forrester, and others want for Jojo.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Maybe a female, or a compatible male.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "It would be good for him to have a companion," says keeper Makaba.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Because being alone is like being cut off from the world - it's like being in prison.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in British Columbia (file image) Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: All four were destroyed "in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines" to protect the public, BCCOS Inspector Jeff Tyre said in an update on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada "Evidence from the investigation as well as animal DNA was analysed and conclusively linked to a sow and its three offspring," he added.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: The attack "likely involved predatory behaviour", which Tyre said was "very rare".
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: He added that more than a dozen conservation officers took part in the investigation over the past week, amid "difficult terrain and weather".
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh, told CBC.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: "When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: Tyre said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a 2025 attack on a school group also in the Bella Coola area.
sentences.article_title: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

sentences.text: Plants and trees from hotter parts of the world are being brought into Sussex Gardeners in one of the most drought-hit parts of the UK have said they are adapting their planting strategies amid increasingly extreme weather.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: West Sussex - like most of the country - experienced an unprecedented summer marked by record-breaking heatwaves and severe drought.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The conditions have put immense stress on many traditional plant species, with some seriously struggling or dying completely.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Iain Parkinson, head of landscape and horticulture at Kew Wakehurst near Ardingly, said he had seen a "big change" in climate over the some 40 years he has worked there.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "We've had trees die," he added.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Meanwhile, senior gardener at High Beeches near Haywards Heath, Elliot Chandler, said some rhododendrons had died off this year.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's probably going to continue," he said.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "We'll do what we can for the plants...but if they're not surviving, then we need to plant different things.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's the only way we can really maintain the garden and keep it full of interest and flowers." This year's heat and lack of rainfall were unprecedented Joe Whelan, head gardener at Nymans in Handcross, warned another year of drought could be "quite detrimental" on larger, more mature trees.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The gardeners said planting a greater diversity of species will be key to climate resilience, with plants from North America, southeastern Europe, central Asia, South Korea and Japan potentially faring better in future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Chandler added it will not be a case of ripping out old plants and planting new species "in one go" but rather a gradual change over time with a "really diverse mix of things".
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Whelan said it will be difficult to predict what will do well in the future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: It will be about "experimenting and accepting that some things probably aren't going to make it", he continued.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Beavers could be reintroduced to the River Waveney, like the ones pictured here,  that have been living in the River Glaven, Norfolk A river separating two counties could become home to beavers as work begins to explore where a colony could be introduced.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: The River Waveney Trust is in conversation with Natural England and other agencies about potentially reintroducing the river-dwelling mammals along the River Waveney.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: The 59-mile (95km) waterway rises in Redgrave and Lopham Fen in Suffolk and heads east, creating a border between Norfolk and Suffolk as it flows out into the River Yare at Great Yarmouth.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: Ange Lamb, catchment resilience officer, said the upper reaches of the River Waveney and its tributaries could make ideal environments for beavers.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: If successful, beavers could return by 2029.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: Known as river engineers, beavers were native to Britain but they were hunted to extinction by the end of the 16th century.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: Conservationists want to reintroduce them to help boost the health of waterways through their ability to create wetland areas.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: But there are concerns, particularly around dams being built in inappropriate places and their ability to destroy trees.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: Two beaver babies - or kits - were born in the wild in Norfolk for the first time in 500 years at Pensthorpe Natural Park Beavers have been reintroduced already in Norfolk at enclosures at Sculthorpe Moor Nature Reserve near Fakenham, Wild Ken Hill near King's Lynn and on the River Glaven near Holt.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: A pair of beavers have also been spotted in the wild at Pensthorpe Natural Park, which is a short distance downstream from Sculthorpe Moor.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: In Suffolk, a colony was introduced at Little Haugh Hall at Norton, near Bury St Edmunds.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: The River Waveney at Scole Bridge, Scole River Waveney Trust is holding a series of events to discuss the proposals and it hopes to engage with local landowners in Bungay, Palgrave and Eye.
sentences.article_title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney

sentences.text: Lamb added: "Our aim is to ensure that local communities, landowners, anglers and conservation groups have the opportunity to be part of the discussion from the beginning." While talks are beginning, Lamb said it would be years before any decision would be made, which would require a licence from Natural England.

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to create new wildlife habitats to attract wildlife including water vole and turtle doves A 370-acre (150-hectare) area of land on the edge of Cambridge has been returned to the care of the National Trust - for the first time in 60 years.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The area - known as Northfield - runs alongside the opposite side of Quy Road towards Bottisham, seven miles (11km) from the city and close to Anglesey Abbey.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to restore the natural site to create new wildlife habitats and improve community access to green space.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Northfield is a rich natural site with a distinctive fen-edge landscape where low-lying fenland meets the higher chalk ridge Northfield has been acquired by the trust for the first time since the 1960s, following an agreement with the tenants.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The site has a rich natural and cultural heritage as well as a chalk stream, with the trust describing the area as "a distinctive fen-edge landscape where low-lying fenland meets the higher chalk ridge".
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: There is evidence of human activity on the site stretching back thousands of years including the Roman period.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The National Trust said it hoped that, over time, species such as harvest mice, water voles and turtle doves would benefit.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Northfield is the first project within the trust's new masterplan for the area, which forms part of a wider Wicken Fen Vision and long-term initiative to "create a more connected and resilient landscape for wildlife and people stretching from Wicken Fen to the edge of Cambridge".

With Kenya's short rainy season now starting, Shikoli tells the BBC she is afraid - especially following warnings that the El Niño weather phenomenon could bring a new round of flooding.

sentences.text: "I feel like it can kill us.

sentences.text: But the workers have a huge task on their hands.

sentences.text: The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.

sentences.text: Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance.

sentences.text: He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Are we too reliant on big tech companies?
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: A critical Microsoft outage lasting more than 22 hours has raised questions about how heavily vital services rely on a handful of major tech firms.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: The disruption, which affected Microsoft 365 services such as Outlook, was caused by routine automated checks that took some servers offline, overloading the remaining ones with traffic.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: The recovery took nearly a full day while engineers gradually restored services, highlighting how embedded the tech giant's services are in modern society.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: Flora Hamilton, executive director of the Small Business Charter, said the outage was a "stark reminder" of how much firms "rely on digital systems" - like Microsoft Outlook - "to keep their operations running".
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: "For many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), access to email is fundamental to everything from communicating with customers and suppliers to generating income," she said.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: The disruption was not just confined to businesses, but also affected organisations and public institutions around the world.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: Around 430 million people globally use Microsoft 365, and issues were reported across more than 70 countries.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: The fallout from the outage had a wide-ranging effect , knocking out email systems for the US House of Representatives and Australian intelligence agencies, as well as disrupting court systems in Singapore and airline support desks in India.
sentences.article_title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech

sentences.text: A statue of William Shakespeare in his birthplace Stratford-upon-Avon The director of the Shakespeare Institute has said he will resign if plans to move the centre from Stratford-upon-Avon to Birmingham go ahead.

sentences.text: Professor Michael Dobson said he was "very unhappy" with the University of Birmingham's decision to relocate the postgraduate research institute from its historic home at Mason Croft to the university's Edgbaston campus in September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.text: "Stratford has been the place where people come to dream of Shakespeare since the 18th Century," he said.
sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.text: It said the decision is about the Institute's "long-term future" and "current students, including research students, will be supported individually through the transition".
sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.text: It added it would consult the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, local representatives and the wider community in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.text: "It affects academics, but it's not an academic decision in which anybody who works on Shakespeare at the University of Birmingham wishes to agree or go along with," he said.
sentences.article_title: Shakespeare chief threatens to resign over Birmingham move

sentences.text: "For 75 years Birmingham has been the only university in the world teaching and studying Shakespeare in Shakespeare's hometown," he said.

sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: On Monday, disgraced entertainer Russell Brand was jailed for rape and sexual assault.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Twenty-four hours later, author and comedian David Walliams was unmasked and accused of preying on young women.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: By Friday the Metropolitan Police had launched an investigation into further allegations about him.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Also in the last week, Married at First Sight UK has been cancelled following allegations of rape on the hit TV show.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: These are all very different stories, but each can be seen as a major reckoning with abuse of power and culture in the industry.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: So why is this all happening now?
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: In reality, the glut of recent days is something of a coincidence.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: All these revelations began with journalistic investigations that started years ago.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: From my own experience - including in my Panorama on Married at First Sight UK - I know investigations typically take a very long time to reach a conclusion, from initial tip-off, to evidence-gathering, corroboration, getting responses, and eventually reporting.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: "The truth is, these stories have a long build up.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: It can be incredibly difficult to get [them] in the papers," Sunday Times columnist Hadley Freeman told me.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: In the case of Brand, there was then a police investigation too, before an outcome was reached in court.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Together these stories represent the consequences of changes that began years ago, rather than a sudden cultural shift in the entertainment industry.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago.

sentences.text: The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities.

sentences.text: The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo.

sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third overall with 10%, unseating the ANC as winner in the city of Durban, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), led by Julius Malema, once seen as a serious challenge to the ANC, came fourth with 6%.

sentences.text: "This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC," said secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: "We knew this disaster is coming, we're staring at it.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: As we got into elections, the cost of living of our people was too high.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: It is a decline that is concerning, that is how I characterise it." President Cyril Ramaphosa is due to be replaced as ANC leader next year It's a continuing decline for the ANC, which lost its parliamentary majority in the national elections in 2024 for the first time since the end of apartheid in 1994.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: It then had to form a coalition government with a raft of other parties in what is called the Government of National Unity (GNU).
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: While the Democratic Alliance made significant gains in the cities in these local elections, its overall vote share rose only marginally from 22% in 2021, and was below the 27% it gained in 2016.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: Voter turnout was 52%, an increase from 46% in 2021, when elections were held during the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: "This election is delivering a devastating message to the ANC," said political analyst Susan Booysen.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: "These are huge problems," says Booysen, "and have really been affecting the lives of ordinary people, in the suburbs, in the townships, and in very dramatic ways." The big picture looks even more bleak for the ANC.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: The party will elect a new leader next year as Ramaphosa comes to end of his term.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: He is due to stay on as president of the country until the next national elections in 2029, but there are few candidates lined up to succeed him in either role.

sentences.text: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline "It is sort of the end of the liberation movement era in South Africa," said political analyst William Gumede, "and the dominance of the liberation movement since the end of apartheid.

sentences.text: So the ANC is going to be a party that by 2029 could be the second biggest rather than the biggest party.

sentences.text: It may actually spiral into a long period of just total infighting.

sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: "We're moving towards a post-racial voting pattern in South Africa," added Gumede.
sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: South Africa now faces days of local coalition building, with the three metropolitan municipalities in the province of Gauteng, the country's powerhouse, under particular scrutiny.

sentences.text: The ANC may even find itself shut out in the cities of Johannesburg and Pretoria.

sentences.article_title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election

sentences.text: "Essentially, what the voters are saying is: 'Well, the ANC has dominated the last three decades, they didn't use their power to change the society for the good, so we don't want the dominant parties anymore, whether at national level, provincial level, or rather now at a local level.

sentences.text: President Tinubu faces re-election with the cost of living and economic hardship the major issues for many voters Nigeria's President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has launched his re-election manifesto, promising to grow the economy, tackle insecurity and address housing shortages.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: The plan targets 6% annual economic growth by 2031, 78,000 additional security personnel and 200,000 affordable homes.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: Titled From Reform to Prosperity, the manifesto builds on Tinubu's first-term economic reforms, including the removal of the fuel subsidy, which has pushed up living costs.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: Nigeria is due to hold a general election in January 2027, with Peter Obi and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar among Tinubu's main challengers.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: The manifesto, launched on 10 November by his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), reflects the government's bid to win back the trust of Nigerians.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: Elected in 2023, Tinubu undertook a series of economic reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidies, the harmonisation of official and parallel foreign exchange rates, and tax reforms.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: "That manifesto was trying to get Nigeria back on its feet, given the condition of the country at that time, slipping into austerity," Joshua Osiyemi, who heads Tracka, a platform launched by the BudgIT Foundation, which is a non-profit organisation that aims to make government financial data easier to understand.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: The reforms, although considered necessary by some economists, have been painful for many Nigerians.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: "Fuel prices went up, and everything that Nigerians consume skyrocketed," Osiyemi told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: "Most Nigerian families are saying they cannot survive on 10,000 naira [$7.40; £5.50] a day," he said, referring to a survey conducted by his organisation.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: Analysis by Nigeria's International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR) found that the price of imported rice rose by 184% between May 2023, when Tinubu took office, and October 2025.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: Other staples, including beans, garri (cassava flour) and bread, also recorded substantial increases.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: In a sign that the reforms might be starting to pay off, SBM Intelligence, a security risk consulting firm, found that the cost of preparing a pot of jollof rice fell by 11.5% between June and September 2026, the sharpest decline it had recorded in the 10 years it has been running its Jollof Index.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: However, this has not translated into significant relief for most households.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.text: "Nigerians spend more and more of their income on basics," said Ikenna Okonkwo, head of research at SBM Intelligence.
sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?

sentences.article_title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?
